reason: The passage emphasizes corporate equality and unified observance rather than elite superiority. The text explicitly states 'One law shall be for the native-born and for the stranger who dwells among you' (Exodus 12:49), establishing that all covenant members are equally bound to the same ordinances. While Moses and Aaron are designated as specific leaders, the narrative repeatedly emphasizes collective participation: 'All the congregation of Israel shall observe it' and 'All the children of Israel did as the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron.' Even regarding social hierarchies present in the text (servants, hired workers, foreigners), the passage shows that circumcised servants can equally participate in the Passover, demonstrating inclusion based on covenant membership rather than inherent superiority of any elite class. The underlying principle is unity under God's law, not the inherent superiority of the elite.
